reference.provenance: Previously supplied unofficial HyperOS port. This is a comparison reference, not proof of official stock provenance.

verified_current_vendor.method: Read-only inspection of HwcFeatureList after matching its binary hash; no memory writes or injection.

reconstructed_contracts.kernel_effect: Tracks whether an AOD layer is present; changes the display pipeline/PQ state. It is distinct from setting brightness.

reconstructed_contracts.operation: DisplayFeature AIDL sendMessage(13, state, empty string)

reconstructed_contracts.mapping: For the reviewed non-multiple-brightness branch: mode 0 normal, 1 high AOD, 2 low AOD.

reconstructed_contracts.operation: Requests a short drawing wake lock and invalidates the AOD view when changing brightness; brightness and rendering are coordinated.

limitations: These commands have not yet been validated as a complete fix on the ColorOS port.
The reference HyperOS compositor and retained compositor binaries differ; whole-library replacement has not been proposed or performed.
The retained MiHwcExtension notifyLayerFlagToHwc handler returns success without doing the work; its presence alone is not a working AOD bridge.
The native Infinity control was interrupted by a tap wake event; its physical AOD result is inconclusive.
AOD support in the composer does not by itself prove a working end-to-end low-power display path.

prepared_probe.scope: Bounded diagnostic, not a persistent patch
prepared_probe.restoration: Reset brightness mode and layer marker, notify normal display state, wake the display. External timeout recovery is required before running a mutating test.

next_step: Run the bounded protocol test in ColorOS with a recovery watchdog and physical observation. Only then design a persistent event-driven adapter; preserve current screen-on fingerprint behavior.
